top_choice_rationale: P003 credits a nameable original experiment by named people: optical detection of a single NV centre (Wrachtrup, 1997) and its coherent control at room temperature (Jelezko and Wrachtrup, 2004), a tabletop result reproduced in very many laboratories that opened a door to solid-state quantum sensing. The narrow citation keeps the attribution clean at two names and avoids claiming the later register and sensing programme. P001 (optical lattice clock) is a close second on maturity and independent verification, but follows two earlier precision-measurement prizes and the redefinition of the second is still a prospect. P002 is a prediction plus decisive experiment but has an unresolved pairing mechanism and omits Cao and Fatemi. P004 adds a sole-laureate IceCube part whose attribution to one person is harder to defend. No award ranks last because the scientific records are real.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; I have no known collaboration with the credited names, and my Chalmers colleague Johansson's flagged B004 is not in this slate. General sympathy for instrument-driven discoveries as an electron microscopist is noted.
